messages:
DeployBot: Scheduled maintenance window booked for eu-west-1 dedicated GPU pools. Change window: 2025-05-18 00:00 - 02:00 UTC. Purpose: kernel patch + driver refresh. Expected: rolling host-level restarts, gradual model pin fallback. Notifying impacted customers via status page and email.

Maya (support): thanks. Can we get a short statuspage snippet + a longer email template for account teams? Also list affected customer tiers.

Sam (oncall): ordering: canary -> regional -> full. Please ensure we run a single canary host in eu-west-1 at T+10m and hold for 20m. If any model-serving errors spike >3% we abort.

Anna (eng-platform): planned pinning: models in the Dedicated v2 pool will be pinned to the prior runtime version for the duration of the window. We'll apply automatic fallback to cpu for low-priority jobs. Need exact model list from inventory.

Liz (product): customer-facing wording note: avoid "downtime" — say "short service restarts for maintenance" and emphasize fallback/continuity. Also include contact path for high-severity customers.

Jai (ops): I'll draft statuspage and email snippets here. Ops will publish a brief statuspage update at T-3 hours and another at T+15 minutes.

Maya (support): paste the snippets pls. we'll localize later.

Jai (ops): Statuspage short (one-line):

```
Scheduled maintenance: Short maintenance & rolling host restarts in our eu-west-1 Dedicated GPU pools. Some customers may see transient request retries during 2025-05-18 00:00-02:00 UTC. No data loss expected. More info: support@redwood.ai
```

Longer email / customer notice (support teams can copy-paste):

```
Hello <CustomerName>,

We are performing scheduled maintenance on our eu-west-1 Dedicated GPU infrastructure on 18 May 2025 between 00:00 and 02:00 UTC. During this window we will apply a kernel and driver patch. This will involve rolling host restarts that may cause brief request retries or increased latency for workloads pinned to Dedicated capacity. Customers using Dedicated v2 pools may see short reconnections; high-availability fallbacks are in place and data is preserved.

What you need to know:
- Window: 2025-05-18 00:00 - 02:00 UTC
- Impact: transient retries / short latency spikes for some requests; no planned data loss
- Mitigation: automatic model pinning and CPU fallback for non-critical queues; canary validation prior to full rollout
- Contact: reply to this message or open a ticket at support@redwood.ai for urgent issues

If your workloads are extremely latency-sensitive during this time, please contact your account team and we can discuss options to reschedule or provide temporary capacity in a different region.

Thanks,
Redwood Support & Ops
```

Sam (oncall): add this to runbook: canary host logs: `/var/log/inference/serving.log` and simple grep for "kv-cache-fault" spikes. If found, abort and roll back.

Anna (eng-platform): also add a quick internal note to the rollout config:

```
rollout_strategy: canary_then_staggered
canary_window_mins: 20
stagger_step_mins: 10
pin_models: true
fallback_priority: cpu-first-for-background
```

Maya (support): good. One more ask: can we include a tiny statuspage timeline snippet for pinned models? something like "Pinned models will remain on prior runtime until 01:00 UTC"

Jai (ops): done — include this in the T-3hr post.

Liz (product): approved wording. Add note for account teams: "If concerned, request a dedicated channel and we'll provide live updates during the window."

DeployBot: Maintenance scheduled by @eng-platform. Reminder set for 3 hours before window start. Reaction :white_check_mark:
